textbookText: Table: 10.1.2 Wetlands of global importance (Ramsar Sites) of Nepal

Benefits of Wetlands Besides recreational and educational benefits, studying wetlands helps us understand their importance in sustaining life and ecosystems. Following are a few benefits of wetland: i.Wetlands foster rich and diverse ecosystems, providing habitats for various plant and animal species. ii.They act as natural buffers, absorbing and storing excess water during heavy rainfall, helping prevent floods. iii.Wetlands filter and purify water by trapping pollutants and sediments, contributing to improved water quality. iv.Wetlands offer opportunities for recreational activities such as bird watching, fishing, and ecotourism. v.They play a role in climate regulation by storing carbon and helping to mitigate the impacts of climate change. vi.Wetlands are often fertile areas suitable for agriculture, supporting crops and sustaining livelihoods. vii.Many threatened and endangered species rely on wetlands for their survival, making them crucial for biodiversity conservation. viii.Studying wetlands enhances our understanding of ecosystems, biodiversity, and environmental science. ix.Vegetation in wetlands helps stabilize soil, preventing erosion and maintaining the integrity of surrounding landscapes. x.Wetlands hold cultural value for many communities, often being sites of historical importance and traditional practices.

The term "simsar", in Nepali, refers to wetland indicating an area with a continuous water source, including rice fields, waterlogged zones, and ponds. Currently, Nepal has ten Ramsar sites, covering 5.5% of the country, recognized for their international importance under the Ramsar Convention. The Ramsar Convention (intergovernmental environmental treaty),

established in 1971 by UNESCO and named after the city of Ramsar in Iran, aims to protect wetlands globally. It is the first treaty for conserving natural resources, focusing on halting wetland loss and managing remaining ones wisely through international collaboration, policymaking, capacity building, and technology transfer.
